entries.markdown:
The IDE is divided into sections.  You can use `Tab` and `Shift + Tab` to move between them.  The sections are:

* Activity bar
* Activity content (if shown)
* Code, costumes/backdrops, sounds pane
* Output, errors and devices pane (if shown)
* Project controls
* Project stage
* Stage and sprites pane

Some of these sections contain more than one tab-stop.  For example, a show/hide button or an "add" button.

The IDE is divided into sections.  You can use `Tab` and `Shift + Tab` to move between them.  The sections are:

* Activity bar
* Activity content (if shown)
* Code editor
* Output, errors and devices pane (if shown)
* Project controls
* Project stage
* Images and sounds pane

Some of these sections contain more than one tab-stop.  For example, a show/hide button or an "add" button.

entries.help: Focus the next major section of the IDE
Focus the previous major section of the IDE

entries.markdown: Tabbing to a particular section can be slow.  You can directly focus some sections with these shortcuts.

entries.help: Focus the **help** area, to refer to help or read a tutorial
Focus the **sprites and stage** area, to choose which sprite (or the stage) to work with
Focus the **coding** area, to work with code, costumes, backdrops, or sounds
Focus the **assets** (images and sounds) area
Focus the **code** editor

entries.markdown: Many things in the IDE have menus attached to them.  For example, a Sprite's menu includes entries to go to its code, costumes, or sounds, and also entries to rename or delete that Sprite.
Many things in the IDE have menus attached to them.  For example, an image's menu includes entries to crop or scale, or rename, or delete that image.

entries.help: Open or close the focused item's menu
Close the menu
Focus the previous / next item in the open menu
Focus the first / last item in the open menu
Choose the focused menu item

entries.markdown: Some areas of the IDE are made up of *tabbed content*, where you choose which content to display from a small set of options.  For example, the *Information* pane has *Output*, *Errors* and *Devices* tabs.

entries.help: Select the previous tabbed content
Select the next tabbed content
Focus the selected content (if possible)

entries.markdown: Vertically down the left-hand edge of the IDE is the "activity bar".  This lets you work with the Scratch-to-Python help information, the tutorial (if you're following one), or this keyboard shortcuts help information.

entries.help: Focus the previous activity tab (help, tutorial, etc.)
Focus the next activity tab (help, tutorial, etc.)
Collapse or expand the activity for the focused tab

entries.markdown: If you know how to do something in Scratch, you can look up the matching Pytch method here.  Or you can just browse the Pytch methods to see how to do something.  As in Scratch, the methods are grouped into sections, which can be expanded or collapsed.  Each method has its own help text, including an example of how to use that method.

entries.help: Focus the previous section or entry
Focus the next section or entry
Collapse or expand the focused section or entry

sections.heading: Working with scripts, costumes, backdrops, sounds

entries.markdown: You can focus the whole script, which lets you do things like move it, delete it, or change its hat block.  To edit a script's code, you first focus the code itself.  While editing code, the `Tab` key is used by the editor to change indentation.  To escape the "tab trap" and return focus to the whole script, use the `Escape` key.

entries.help: Focus the actual code of the focused script so you can edit its code
Focus the whole script, not its code, so you can work with the whole script

entries.markdown: You can focus the whole coding area as part of tabbing around the IDE.  To edit your code, you first focus the code itself.  While editing code, the `Tab` key is used by the editor to change indentation.  To escape the "tab trap" and return focus to the whole coding area, use the `Escape` key.

entries.help: Focus the actual code of your project so you can edit the code
Focus the coding area, not the code, so you can go back to navigating the IDE with the keyboard
Show autocomplete suggestions after `self.` or `pytch.`
Increase / decrease the indentation of current line or selected lines

entries.markdown: If you are following a tutorial, there is a navigation area which shows "buttons" for the chapters.  For space reasons, sometimes not all chapter buttons are shown, but as you navigate, more are revealed.

entries.help: Focus the previous chapter button
Focus the next chapter button
Switch to and focus the chapter for the focused button
